description: Upscale a finished video on fal — a kept Stage sitting (or its scored version) or an Editor Deliver render — to a higher resolution. Read list_upscales first: it names every video that can be upscaled (`source` ids like `sitting:<id>`, `scored:<id>`, `render:<file>`), the models, and which resolutions each model offers. This SPENDS the author's fal credits and a 4K pass on a long film is not cheap, so confirm the video, model and resolution with the author before calling it unless they already named all three. It only STARTS the job: the upscale runs on fal for minutes, so poll it with get_upscale (the job id this returns) until status is `done` — the finished file is then copied into the project and the original is never touched.

source.description: The video to upscale, exactly as list_upscales names it: `sitting:<sittingId>` (a kept Stage sitting), `scored:<sittingId>` (that sitting's scored version) or `render:<file>` (an Editor Deliver render).

model.description: The upscaler. `seedvr` (SeedVR2) = diffusion restoration, the sharpest on AI-generated footage and the only one offering 720p. `bytedance` = ByteDance's video upscaler, fast and clean with an AIGC preset. `topaz` = Topaz Proteus, the conservative choice that invents the least detail.

resolution.description: The target height. 2160p is 4K. Pick one the chosen model offers (list_upscales says which).

sourceHeight.description: The source video's height in pixels, when known. Only Topaz uses it (it upscales by a FACTOR, so the factor is target ÷ source). Omitted, the source is assumed to be 720p.
